Note::diff_chars¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::diff_chars(const Note& other) const

Character-Level Difference Between Two Notes¶

diff_chars(other) compares each cell of self against the matching cell of other one character at a time and returns only the changes as a TokenBatch of tag-prefixed tokens. It is the finest-grained member of the diff / align family; the coarser ones are nlp().diff_words(), diff_lines, and (sentence granularity, with equal tokens) nlp().align_sentences().

How the comparison works¶

Each cell pair is split into characters, and the two character lists are aligned by their longest common subsequence. Because diff_chars is a diff_* method, only the characters that differ are emitted — one per token, in reading order, with a one-byte tag:

Tag

Meaning

In self

In other

-

removed — in self, not matched in other

yes

no

+

added — in other, not matched in self

no

yes

The tag is the first byte of the token; the character follows. Characters common to both sides produce no token, so a cell whose two sides are identical contributes an empty range. For the full transcript that keeps the unchanged characters as well, run nlp().align_tokens(), but note that aligns words, not characters; there is no equal-included character spelling, so reconstruct from the -/+ stream and the original text when you need one.

Splitting is by Unicode character, not raw byte: a multi-byte character such as é or 🎯 is one token, tag included.

The TokenBatch result¶

Tokens from all cells are concatenated into the rank-1 Note batch.tokens(). The rank-1 Int64 Note batch.offsets() has length numel + 1 and marks each cell’s run: cell r owns tokens.at(k) for k in [offsets[r], offsets[r + 1]). An unchanged cell’s range is empty (offsets[r] == offsets[r + 1]).

Shape, pairing, and rejections¶

Comparison is per cell and pairwise. self and other must share numel, or one may be a scalar (numel() == 1) broadcast against the other. Rejections raise pluss::Error:

  • bytes-mode self → Note::diff_chars requires a UTF-8 text Note (lhs is bytes).

  • unequal numel, neither side scalar → Note::diff_chars expects equal numel or scalar broadcast.

The alignment is O(m · n) in characters per cell — practical for words, identifiers, and short strings; for long documents prefer nlp().diff_words() or diff_lines. It is deterministic: on a tie the - is emitted before the +.

Example 1: A Character Edit Script¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"kitten"})
                       .diff_chars(pluss::make_note({"sitting"}));

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[5], dim=1, numel=5, encoding=utf8)
["-k", "+s", "-e", "+i", "+g"]
offsets: [0, 5]

k → s, e → i, then a trailing g is inserted; itt and n are shared and produce nothing.

Example 2: A Pure Insertion¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"abc"})
                       .diff_chars(pluss::make_note({"abXYZc"}));
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["+X", "+Y", "+Z"]

Only + tokens — nothing was removed from self.

Example 3: Identical Cells Produce Nothing¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"same"})
                       .diff_chars(pluss::make_note({"same"}));
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]
offsets: [0, 0]

An empty token Note and an empty range for the one cell.
